sections.heading: Fiji head coach vacancy sees Jake White emerge as favourite
sections.body: Former South Africa head coach Jake White has emerged as the favourite to take over Fiji ahead of their upcoming November internationals. Reports from South African newspaper Rapport indicate that the 2007 World Cup winner is the preferred candidate among 31 applicants to succeed Mick Byrne. White, who last worked with the Bulls, recently expressed his desire for an international return, stating, 'I still think I have unfinished business at the Test level.' The Fiji Rugby Union is expected to announce the appointment shortly.

lead.why: Former Springboks boss Jake White has reportedly emerged as the frontrunner for the vacant Fiji head coaching role.

sections.heading: Maika Sivo is omitted from Mick Potter's Fiji league World Cup squad
sections.body: Fiji league head coach Mick Potter has named his 23-man squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup, with Leeds Rhinos winger Maika Sivo a major omission. Sivo, the Super League's top try-scorer in 2026, missed the club's run-in with arm and shoulder injuries, though his exclusion is not yet confirmed as injury-related. The squad features Super League players Semi Valemei, Waqa Blake, Taane Milne and new Warrington signing Mitchell Prest. The Bati face Cook Islands, Australia and New Zealand in Pool A.

lead.why: It is a highly notable squad announcement for the upcoming tournament, featuring a major star omission.

sections.heading: Jake White emerges as the favourite for vacant Fiji job
sections.body: Jake White has emerged as the leading contender to replace Mick Byrne as Fiji head coach, with a source telling Afrikaans outlet Rapport, "He is on their shortlist and is regarded as the favourite." The former Springboks World Cup-winning coach, now a consultant at Selborne College, is among 31 applicants including Warren Gatland. Fiji are due to confirm Byrne's successor in the coming days, with the new boss set to take charge for November's Nations Championship fixtures against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: A specific frontrunner naming Jake White as favourite is a real development on the coaching search, not just a rehash of yesterday's applicant list.

sections.heading: RFU set to offer England head coach Steve Borthwick contract extension
sections.body: The RFU is set to offer England head coach Steve Borthwick a contract extension that will secure his position beyond next year's World Cup. While Borthwick's tenure has faced scrutiny for being full of tactical contradictions, the union is moving to finalise a deal that offers stability. Former England international Ben Kay insisted Borthwick’s side can reach the standard required to win the tournament, provided the head coach addresses key areas including midfield selection and club relationships ahead of the upcoming autumn campaign.

sections.heading: Brain injury claimants still face £2.8m bill to continue case
sections.body: No fresh line on this today. sections.heading: Josh Adams eyes fitness return for Wales' autumn internationals after injury
sections.body: Josh Adams says he will be fit for Wales' autumn internationals after the calf injury that ruled him out of July's 43-0 defeat by South Africa in Durban. The Cardiff wing has missed the start of the season but is training again, with a club return expected this month. Adams, the leading try-scorer at the 2019 World Cup, is targeting a third global tournament, in Australia next year. "I am training, but it's important that you navigate your way through correctly and there's no rush," he said.

sections.heading: Argentina launches ambitious joint bid to host 2035 Rugby World Cup
sections.body: Argentina has officially launched a historic four-nation bid alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil to host the men's 2035 Rugby World Cup. The Argentine Rugby Union is leading the proposal, which would bring the tournament to South America for the first time. Technical details have been submitted to World Rugby, listing eight Argentine venues including Buenos Aires' Monumental and José Amalfitani stadiums, alongside Rio de Janeiro’s iconic Maracanã. World Rugby will select the preferred host in May 2027.

sections.heading: Argentina joins Uruguay, Chile and Brazil in 2035 World Cup bid
sections.body: Argentina has formally joined Uruguay, Chile and Brazil in a joint bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, submitting technical information to World Rugby. The Argentine Rugby Union is leading the four-nation proposal, which would stage matches across all four countries — among the venues offered are the Monumental and José Amalfitani Stadium in Buenos Aires alongside Rio's Maracanã. No South American nation has previously hosted the men's tournament. World Rugby expects to name a preferred host in May 2027, with the Council's final vote in November 2027.

lead.why: Freshest, most corroborated story in today's pack and not previously covered, unlike the recent run of log/ranking editions.

sections.heading: Japan Sakura XV finish winless in Europe after second Ireland defeat
sections.body: The Japan Sakura XV return home from their European tour winless after falling 43-19 to Ireland in Cork on Saturday. Despite a strong start that saw Sakurako Korai score from an early rolling maul to take an initial lead, Japan struggled to contain the Irish pack and were forced into a challenging defensive position. The side now turns its attention to a two-Test home series against Wales in the WXV Global Series, beginning later this month.

lead.why: It reports on the conclusion of the Sakura XV's recent tour, providing a definitive update on their status following their latest result.

sections.heading: Nel Metcalfe returns to Wales squad for double-header against Japan
sections.body: Full-back Nel Metcalfe has been named in the Wales squad for their upcoming WXV double-header against the Japan Sakura XV. The 21-year-old Gloucester-Hartpury player returns to the international setup following a knee injury that ruled her out of the 2026 Women's Six Nations. Wales are scheduled to face the hosts at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo on 24 October, before the sides meet again seven days later at Kumagaya Rugby Stadium in Saitama Prefecture.

sections.heading: Nel Metcalfe returns as Wales women name squad for Japan tour

Co-captains Alex Callender and Kate Williams lead a 30-strong party that includes uncapped props Stella Orrin and Crystal James, fresh off beating South Africa before narrowly losing to the USA. Lynn said: 'We asked the players to move the dial, and we did that in those two Test matches.'

sections.heading: Jason Ryan admits Springboks 'sucked a lot of juice' out All Blacks
sections.body: New Zealand scrum coach Jason Ryan has conceded that the gruelling four-Test series against the Springboks left his squad physically and mentally drained. Reflecting on the 3-1 series defeat, Ryan admitted that the world champions exposed significant vulnerabilities in the All Blacks' set-piece, particularly regarding opposition ball. “The tour sucked a lot of juice out of everyone,” Ryan said. The New Zealand camp is now focused on rectifying these scrum issues ahead of their upcoming Bledisloe Cup matches against Australia.

lead.why: The All Blacks coaching staff have publicly admitted the physical toll and set-piece dominance exerted by the Springboks during their recent series.

sections.heading: Jason Ryan admits Springboks scrum exposed All Blacks' set-piece flaws
sections.body: All Blacks scrum coach Jason Ryan has given the Springboks' set-piece a rousing verdict after South Africa's 3-1 series win, admitting the tourists exposed glaring weaknesses in New Zealand's defensive scrum. Ryan said the four-Test series "sucked a lot of juice out of everyone" and that seven scrum penalties proved costly at crucial moments. Lock Scott Barrett, who missed the series through surgery, backed the assessment, praising the Boks' scrum-to-maul platform as the engine of their dominance — a theme now shaping New Zealand's Bledisloe Cup preparation against Australia.

lead.why: Fan-friendliest story: an All Blacks coach publicly conceding the Boks' scrum exposed New Zealand's weaknesses, with corroborating detail from Barrett and Kirwan.
